name: Schwaz
kurzbeschreibung: The medieval Silberstadt – once the heart of European mining with the largest Silberbergwerke.
beschreibung:
Overview

Schwaz is situated at an elevation of 545 meters in the Lower Inn Valley, approximately 30 kilometers east of Innsbruck at the base of Mount Kellerjoch (2,344 m). With roughly 14,500 residents, the historic district capital is the cultural and economic heart of the Silberregion Karwendel. Known globally as the Silver City, Schwaz flourished during the 15th and 16th centuries into the Habsburg Empire’s second-largest city after Vienna, powered by rich silver and copper mines. Today, splendid late Gothic townhouses, medieval arcades, Freundsberg Castle, and the Franciscan Monastery reflect its glittering past, harmoniously blending mining heritage with modern urban vibrancy and Alpine outdoor recreation in the Tux and Karwendel Alps.

History

First recorded in 930/931 as Sûates, Schwaz rose to international fame after 1409 when, according to legend, the maidservant Gertraud Kandlerin discovered a silver vein exposed by a bull on Falkenstein hill. Schwaz soon became known as the Mother of all Mines, yielding up to 85 percent of the world's silver. The wealth financed Emperor Maximilian I and was managed by the Augsburg banking houses of Fugger and Welser. Renaissance figures such as Paracelsus and poet Hans Sachs worked here. The Parish Church of the Assumption, constructed between 1490 and 1502, is Tyrol’s largest hall church, roofed with over 15,000 copper tiles. The Franciscan Monastery, established in 1507, features renowned Gothic passion and dance-of-death frescoes. Following destruction in the 1809 Tyrolean uprising, Schwaz was chartered as a city in 1899 by Emperor Franz Joseph I.

Getting there

Schwaz boasts exceptional transport links. Motorists use the A12 Inntal autobahn via exit 39 (Schwaz) or the B171 federal road. By rail, Schwaz railway station is serviced every 20 to 30 minutes by Tyrolean S-Bahn lines S4 and S5 running between Innsbruck and Kufstein. The nearby transit hub in Jenbach (5 km away) provides direct connections to Austrian Federal Railways (ÖBB) Railjet and Eurocity international services. Local bus networks connect the town center to the surrounding villages, Pillberg, and the Kellerjoch lift.

Tips

Tour the Schwaz Silver Mine, riding an authentic miner's train 800 meters underground into the 1491 Sigmund gallery to witness historical water pumps and timbered shafts. Visit Freundsberg Castle for local history exhibits in its tower and sweeping views over the Inn Valley. Experience the digital night sky shows at the Zeiss Planetarium. For mountain adventures, take the Kellerjoch chairlift to hike to the Kellerjoch hut and summit chapel, or stroll through the historic town center to admire the Franciscan cloister frescoes.
